title: Harry Maguire found guilty of non-serious assault, has suspended sentence reduced
content:
Harry Maguire has been found guilty of non-serious assault and handed a suspended 15-month sentence in a retrial of his 2020 Mykonos case.

Allegations against Maguire were heard once again in the Greek court system on Wednesday, with the retrial held at fifth time of asking following years of delays.

The 32-year-old’s original 21-month suspended sentence was reduced in length and severity by the court and a fine was also removed.

Maguire intends to appeal the retrial’s verdict in Greece’s Supreme Civil and Criminal Court, to quash the judgement. The England international has consistently refused to settle the case because he is determined to clear his name.

Maguire was arrested following an altercation on a family holiday on the Greek island of Mykonos in August 2020.

The former United captain and his brother, Joe Maguire, were found guilty of offences including attempted bribery, repeated bodily harm and violence against public employees.

Chris Sharman, a friend of the family, was also convicted on the same charges with the exception of attempted bribery. All three men denied the charges.

Harry Maguire was originally handed a 21-month jail sentence, suspended for three years, but the conviction was quashed on appeal only a day after his initial sentencing.

The England international was granted a full retrial by the Greek courts, but that hearing was subsequently postponed on four occasions, most recently in October last year.

Maguire was not required to attend the retrial on the island on Syros on Wednesday and the development does not affect his availability for United’s Premier League meeting with Newcastle United on Wednesday evening.

Maguire is a doubt for the trip to St James’ Park due to illness, having been brought off in the 85th minute of Sunday’s 2-1 win over Crystal Palace.
